result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): The two answers are close. Both propose an editable read of the question before Start, an early checkpoint that continues if the client doesn't answer, findings-based progress and per-claim verification tags. A is stronger on mid-run steering: Pause/Stop keeps finished work, only the affected phase is rerun, and single sections can be redone. A also explicitly says it has no figures. B is better at making the report open with a one-page answer, while A's opening page covers confidence and gaps rather than the answer. B's example counts ('41 claims: 29 confirmed...') are a format mock-up, not a claim about Deepfield, but they come close to the line. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers propose an editable interpretation step, an early checkpoint that continues if the client doesn't reply, findings-based progress and per-claim evidence tags. B goes further on mid-run control: Pause and Stop that keep finished work, redirects that rerun only the affected phase, immediate problem alerts and section-level redo. A is the only one that explicitly says the report should open with a one-page answer. Neither invents Deepfield statistics: A's claim counts are clearly illustrative, and B says outright that it has no baseline figure.
